Next, option B: "Plants make their own food." This is about photosynthesis. Historically, people didn't understand how plants make food. I remember learning that before, it was thought that plants got their nutrients from the soil. But then, through experiments, scientists discovered that plants need light, water, and air to make their own food, which is glucose. So when new experiments provided evidence, this conclusion changed. That makes B a strong candidate.

Moving on to option C: "The Sun revolves around Earth." This was a common belief until the invention of the telescope. Galileo challenged this idea when he provided evidence that the Earth revolves around the Sun. However, the statement itself is now known to be false because the Sun is much larger and the Earth revolves around it. But does this statement change because of new information? Well, once it was proven, it stopped being accepted, but it wasn't a conclusion that scientists changed because new info became available; it was a belief that was disproven. So maybe C is a contender, but I think the reasoning is a bit different.

Putting it all together, the statement that changed because new information became available is B) Plants make their own food. This was due to experimental evidence from scientists like van Helmont, Priestley, and Ingenhousz who demonstrated how plants synthesize their own food through photosynthesis.
